message:
feat(task-050): the signing session read model publishes how the envelope ended

GET /api/v1/signing/session now carries envelope_outcome (AGREED or NOT_AGREED,
always present, null until the envelope closes), from the same rule the gate
uses. The signer goes straight from the auth step to the read model and needs
it there. HTTP tests cover the waybill, board and courtesy-copy delivery cases.

refactor(task-050): drop the quorum readers and bound min_signatures

Step::isQuorumStep() and isQuorumMet() lost their last caller with the
Session refusal they served, so they go. SESSION_CLOSED now says a released
leg, not the sender, closed the session. A min_signatures past the INT column
answers 422 naming the field instead of failing at the insert.

Merge feat/envelope-expiry: an envelope expires at its date

TASK-049 brings the per-minute sweep that closes an envelope at its date
through the ending rules.

Merge feat/deadline-bars: close-now and the envelope expiry join the step policy

Brings TASK-049's expiry (expires_at, the clock sweep, EnvelopeExpiredException)
into the step-policy work of TASK-050.

test(task-050): close-now and no-deadline expiry are covered over HTTP

A sender's close-now releases the pending members of a secured AT_LEAST step
and is idempotent. The waybill with no deadline on the consignee step expires
agreed, and expiry closes every reachable step combination as the other endings do.

fix(task-050): an act past its step's deadline answers LEG_CLOSED

STEP_DEADLINE_PASSED went through the admission untranslated and reached the
client as an unpublished refusal. Ending stories now play step deadlines, vetoes
and close-now against the aggregate, and the order of a step's completion and
its releases is pinned.
docs(task-051): ADR-0074 proposes one answer for a closed envelope or leg

feat(task-050): a step's deadline is stored at activation and swept when due

The deadline instant is stored on the step when it activates (ADR-0073 section 2.13).
A clock's releases are judged as of its own instant, and the sender cannot end
an envelope while a due step is waiting to be swept.
Merge feat/step-policy: gate fields, revocation and the deadline seam join the package

fix(task-051): an act past an unswept step deadline answers what the sweep will make of it

ADR-0074 is accepted: it supersedes ADR-0067 sections 2.3 and 7.3 and amends
ADR-0066 section 2.6. In the deadline gap an act answers ENVELOPE_NO_LONGER_LIVE
or LEG_CLOSED. The task record is corrected where it misdescribed the gate routes.

fix(task-050): a leg the gate no longer admits cannot open or read documents

A member whose leg closed while the envelope stayed open could still open their
link, or read bytes on a session credential minted before the close. The opening
is now refused under the row lock and mints nothing, and
ENVELOPE_NO_LONGER_LIVE no longer tells a recipient the document was cancelled.

fix(task-051): a closed envelope or leg answers before the session's own state

On every act and gate route, the code a recipient gets on a closed envelope or
leg no longer depends on whether a revocation has run (ADR-0074 sections 2.1-2.4).

fix(task-051): an informational member gets its role refusal in the deadline gap

A VIEWER, REVIEWER or EDITOR acting in the step-deadline gap answers its role
refusal. The published 409s now state the same answer before and after the
revocation, an HTTP test holds it, and ADR-0074 names the tests that enforce it.

Merge feat/deadline-bars: late openings are refused on a closed leg

The opening is refused under the row lock on a closed leg and the bytes cut is
synchronous.

test(task-050): the waybill and the board end at their step deadline over HTTP

Delivery-bar cases (g) and (h), driven with the real sweep and a pinned clock.

test(task-050): a step deadline releases the silent consignee and opens the closing step

Delivery-bar cases (d) and (e) on the waybill with a fourth closing step, driven
by the real sweep; an unclaimed slot's release ends the envelope.
Merge feat/deadline-bars: delivery-bar cases (d) and (e) over HTTP

docs(task-051): the OTP send, decline re-auth and SESSION_CLOSED text match the routes

Addresses three contract-check warnings on the published responses.

Merge feat/step-policy: a step says how much agreement it needs, with veto and deadline

Sits on top of expiry and the ending rules. Conflicts in the docs index and the
EnvelopeVoided event were resolved keeping both sides.

docs(task-050): the domain models and ADR-0073 state the step policy and close-now

The models describe CloseEnvelopeNow, the step-deadline sweep and the revocation
that spares readers. ADR-0073 lists what TASK-050 made true and the records it
amends carry the amendment.

docs(task-050): a void spares sessions whose gate still passes

The decision is published on the route and recorded as load-bearing. A new test
shows tenant B's key cannot close or void tenant A's envelope. The opening's
fail-open docblock and signer.role (a VIEWER is published as REVIEWER) are corrected.
docs(task-050): two read-after-close tests no longer say close-now has no entry point
Merge feat/task-048-how-an-envelope-ends: TASK-050's close joins the package fixes

docs(adr): ADR-0057's quorum-unreachable measurement is dated 2026-08-25

Quorum steps are authorable now, so the claim that none could be authored holds
only as of that date.
test(task-050): the released-signer case no longer denies close-now and the clocks
Merge docs/package-handoffs: the TASK-050 handoffs are official
Merge feat/package-fixes: security and contract fixes from the join

fix(envelope): an invitation's sent and failed instants keep their microseconds

DbalEnvelopeRepository wrote invitation_sent_at and invitation_failed_at through
a type that truncated them. The no-deadline waybill case (j) now gets its two
release reasons from the envelope's two lives instead of a resend.
Merge feat/package-fixes: invitation instants keep microseconds, case (j) is deterministic

Merge feat/task-048-how-an-envelope-ends: expiry, ending notice, step policy, LEG_CLOSED

Brings the ADR-0073 package (TASK-048, 049, 040, 050).

fix(task-051): a closed leg or unswept deadline is answered as the sweep will leave it

Three fixes found at the join of TASK-051 with the ADR-0073 package, kept in one
commit because they share the predicate path.

docs(task-051): the records describe the opening's refusal and the step-deadline gap

The step-deadline gap is read from the envelope's pure clock decision. The
Envelope and Session models and ADR-0074 section 5 name what enforces it on the
opening and every gate route.

Merge develop: ADR-0072's audit trail joins the ADR-0073 package

Conflicts resolved keeping both sides; develop's backlog rows BL-310..324 came first.

Merge feat/envelope-answers-first: a closed envelope or leg answers the same (ADR-0074)

TASK-051 branched before develop's evidence-audit merge; two textual conflicts
were resolved keeping both sides.

docs: authoring rules are cited as the repo's own, not by the file that holds them

About thirty citations added by the package named the operational guide's file.

Merge feat/task-048-how-an-envelope-ends: how an envelope ends, one answer after revoke

Brings TASK-048, 049, 040, 050 and 051: a sent envelope always reaches a closing.

build(infection): the mutation run finishes instead of dying in its own cleanup

At about 15000 mutants the master process ran out of its 512M. Two conservation
tests now read their own trails whatever other tests committed, and the ending
crossings remove the audit trails they commit.

Merge chore/infection-memory: the mutation run reaches its verdict

Infection's master gets 1536M and a clean temp dir, so it no longer dies before
the minimum-MSI check.

test: the test environment writes into its own buckets and broker vhost

Tests wrote real bytes that no rollback removes into the dev buckets, and the
opt-in AMQP transport used the same queues the dev worker consumes.

Merge chore/test-buckets: tests no longer write into the dev stack's buckets or queues

Tests use f5sign-test-staging / f5sign-test-retained and the f5sign_test vhost.

feat(notification): emails wear the signer's identity and ask not to be auto-answered

The emails still carried the original wireframe look. They now use the signer's
wordmark and colours, with images served by the signer. Mails carry headers
that suppress out-of-office replies to the no-reply sender.

docs: the records state that the ADR-0073 package is merged and cite commits that exist

The void crossing test keeps its sent fixture unexpired past its fixed date.
BL-192, BL-207 and BL-290 are closed by the package, each checked against develop.

Merge feat/email-signer-identity: the notification emails wear the signer's identity

The FACTOR 5 wordmark, corporate red for identity only, ink for the act.
Merge origin/develop into docs/post-merge-record-drift: signer-identity emails join
Merge docs/post-merge-record-drift: the suite no longer goes red on a past date

feat(evidence-audit): the audit trail ends where the envelope ends, for both outcomes

The trail is issued at ENVELOPE_COMPLETED for either outcome and covers the
envelope's event stream up to that point.

feat(evidence-audit): the audit trail accounts for every party the envelope released

A party's act becomes an outcome with kind SIGNED, DECLINED or RELEASED, so a
released party appears with its cause instead of vanishing.

feat(evidence-audit): the audit trail states the expiry and labels every end cause

The JSON gains envelope.expiry (expires_at, first_expires_at). ADR-0072 records
the re-cut that follows ADR-0073.

fix(evidence-audit): the trail states the ending's outcome and sender as the envelope does

A completion whose outcome is neither AGREED nor absent is stated as an ending
without agreement. The trail's tests, published route text and records are
corrected to say when a trail is issued and what a void closes.

docs: stranded docblocks sit on their own declarations again

28 docblocks move back onto the declaration they describe, and 5 declarations
whose docblock was split in two are rejoined.

fix(signing): a visible mark lands on its box on a rotated page

Placements are authored on the page as displayed, after its /Rotate, which is how
the signer paints them through pdf.js. DSS is now asked to map each box through
the page rotation.

feat(kernel): repository failures become capabilities, with create-once as another

RepositoryFailure and NotFoundFailure replace a second base class, and
IdempotentCreation adds createIfAbsent(), which keeps the stored aggregate. The
repository contract docblock is restyled.

Merge fix/rotated-page-mark: a visible mark lands on its box on a rotated page

DSS now maps each box through its page's /Rotate (rotation AUTOMATIC). BL-366
files placement bounds.

feat(kernel): repositories gain existence probes, locked loads and Result-returning find()

ExistenceProbe and LockedLoad are new capabilities, CapturesFailures lets a
helper return a failure as a value, and Repository::find() may answer with a
Result, adopted one repository at a time.

Merge develop: release v0.0.1 - envelope endings, expiry, step policy, audit trail

Brings from develop since v0.0.0: envelope endings with outcome and end cause
(close now, decline, void), expiry, step policies, and the audit trail re-cut.

feat(foundation): a unit of work a participant can own, and the bus as its default caller

The UnitOfWork port in Foundation/Persistence draws the outermost transaction
boundary, so a use case can own it and the bus opens one by default.

refactor(transactions): transactions opened on the connection move to the unit of work

The session repository's auth methods stop opening their own transactions. A
new PHPStan rule makes the classes that may open a transaction a closed roster.

refactor(envelope): a document's bytes are written after the commit

UploadDocumentBytes owns its unit of work: the use case opens the custody and
records the artifact in the commit, and the bytes follow outside any transaction.

Merge refactor/persistence-incremental: transactions belong to a unit of work

Create-once, existence, locked load and Result-returning find() arrive one at a time.

docs(adr): ADR-0075 proposes answering the signing gate on the act (TASK-052)

A recipient behind an open access gate with any signing method could decline
without the second factor the sender declared.
docs(task-052): ADR-0075 is agreed and its realization is unblocked

feat(session): the signing gate is answered on the act, and a decline passes it

Under a neutral access gate, anyone holding a forwarded link could open the
session, receive a credential and decline. The commit, the decline and the
machine signature route now each pass the signing gate. This part holds the
schema, config, domain, application and adapters.

test(session): cover the signing gate answered on the act

Tests for the commit, decline and machine signature routes passing the signing
gate, including a decline behind a neutral access gate.

feat(evidence-audit): the trail names the act a signing-gate pass and a code sent served

Without it, the first decline behind a signing gate would print a verification
for an act the trail did not name. Also: a stray asserted member on the machine
signature route is refused as an assertion, the machine twin of route 5 declares
its 423 and 429 answers, and TASK-052's handoffs are written.
docs(adr): ADR-0075 is accepted, and the records it amends say so

Merge fix/signing-gate-on-the-act: the signing gate is answered on the act

TASK-052 realizes the now-accepted ADR-0075.

chore(lint): a closure that does not use $this is static

php-cs-fixer's static_lambda rule is on; the closures it found are made static.

docs(adr): ADR-0076 writes a custody's bytes outside every transaction

Adds the kernel capability RecoveryReport so every recovery reports what it did
and the state it left, sealed to Recovered or RecoveryFailure. Option, Result and
the report declare purity, and phpstan/README.md states the convention.

feat(storage): a custody that will never receive bytes is withdrawn

storage.custody.withdrawn_at is set only on a PENDING row and a withdrawn custody
refuses a first write. The object-store client's idle timeout is declared in
config (60 seconds, the value PHP's default gave).

feat(storage): writeAlongside commits with its consumer's record

CustodyStore::writeAlongside() puts the bytes with no transaction open, then
commits the custody's first write in the same transaction as the consumer's record.

refactor(evidence-audit): the trail is registered with its bytes

IssueAuditTrail owns its unit of work, so no transaction is open while the trail
is gathered, rendered and sealed.
docs(adr): ADR-0076 is accepted, and the records it amends say so
Merge refactor/trail-write-after-commit: audit trail bytes land outside transactions

feat(session): a signature image is checked before it is kept, in a table of its own

The image is decoded once to validate it, so the PHP image now builds ext-gd for
PNG only (TASK-053). The mark's image also reaches DSS as {bytes, name}, because
DSS 6.4 refuses a request carrying mimeType.

feat(session): the commit takes a signature image and keeps its digest

POST /api/v1/signing/commit accepts a base64 PNG signature_image, kept until the
recipient's marks are sealed and then cleared. SignatureExecution reads it through
Session's contract, and the session config asks for a drawn signature under
SEQUENTIAL_PADES.

feat(evidence-audit): a mark drawn from a committed image states that image's digest

The session asks for a drawn signature exactly where the commit takes one. An HTTP
test drives a drawn signature to both marks and checks its bytes are then cleared,
and the signer's handoff is written.

fix(session): a signature image must be an 8-bit RGB or RGBA PNG without interlacing

That is what the signer's canvas exports. The image bytes no longer show in stack
frames, and a test now reads back a sealed mark as sound signatures.

docs(task-053): the schema and models describe the recipient's signature image

LIVE_SCHEMA.md lists session.signature_image. A fake's docblock is moved back
onto its method.

Merge feat/drawn-signature-on-mark: a recipient's drawn signature appears on their marks

A SEQUENTIAL_PADES recipient with a visible mark commits a PNG of their signature (TASK-053).

feat(signature-execution): a mark's text is laid out in the lines its box holds

DSS 6.4 draws a mark's text in PT Serif Regular at a fixed size and clips what
does not fit. MarkTextLayout wraps at word boundaries to the box width less 3 pt
of padding a side.

fix(signature-execution): a mark's whole text is drawn inside its box

Measured against DSS 6.4 in the waybill's boxes. consent_biometric_required is
documented as an optional checkbox, not a gate.

Merge fix/mark-text-fits: a mark's whole text is drawn inside its box

A long name lost its start, clipped by DSS, and a drawn signature was stretched.

test(signature-execution): an image alone is drawn centred in its box

Measured against the live DSS, as TASK-054 D11 asks before a mark without a name is offered.

feat(task-054): the sender chooses how each recipient signs and shows their name

Each recipient carries a signature setting authored when added and never corrected
afterwards.

feat(task-054): send refuses SIGNATURE_MODES_NEED_A_MARK; handoffs and live tests land

Handoffs tell the signer and the senders how each recipient signs. Three recipients
sign over HTTP as their settings say and each mark matches. A mark with a hidden
name is the image alone, centred. The send route now publishes the code
Envelope::send() throws.

fix(session): the session offers only the ways a recipient can actually sign

allowed_signature_modes published the sender's offer whole. signature_modes now
takes at most three entries, and the send and commit refusal text states the real order.
docs(task-054): the domain models and ADR index state the signature setting as built

fix(session): a code request the cooldown refuses spends no send budget

The issuance use case charged the hourly send limiter before the aggregate checked
the 60-second interval between codes.

feat(notification): an SMS DSN can name a plaintext local Twilio mock with tls=0

The Twilio transport always used HTTPS, so a dev mock speaking plain HTTP could not
be reached. Dev email and SMS now land in the MessagePit sink.
Merge feat/sms-dsn-plaintext-dev: dev email and SMS land in the MessagePit sink
Merge develop: SMS DSN tls=0, the MessagePit dev sink and the cooldown budget fix

docs(task-031): a recipient declares reachable channels; an unreachable one is shown

A recipient with no email received nothing and nobody was told.

Merge feat/signature-modes: the sender chooses how each recipient signs

Merged with develop and validated there.

fix(identity): a UUID followed by a newline is not canonical

isCanonical() and assertCanonical() now refuse it; before, the pattern's trailing
anchor let it through.

docs: delivery is designed end to end, from declared channel to what the trail shows

Three Proposed records decided together in one design audit (ADR-0077 re-cut, ADR-0078,
ADR-0079). ADR-0078 declares that it amends ADR-0037 decision 7 again, for TASK-056.

docs: TASK-057, 058 and 059 have every decision confirmed and are ready to implement

Owner decisions of 2026-10-09: the SMS resend cap is 5. SMS reaches eight countries (ES, PT,
FR, IT, DE, PL, RO, BG) and a mobile outside them is refused with its own code.

feat(notification): a delivery can end NOT_NEEDED or FAILED transiently

A delivery whose retries run out ends FAILED with a TRANSIENT kind. Its failure kind
and send window are stored, and every existing FAILED row reads as permanent (ADR-0079).

feat(notification): a delivery request carries its retry profile and a code's send window

A purpose answers NOTICE or CODE for its retry profile. Every code request carries a
send window of the resend cooldown, Notification refuses one without it, and a
delivery's message has its own retry schedule.

feat(bus): async_events retries per message; exhausted deliveries end FAILED transiently

ADR-0079 section 2.4: the transport's retry strategy hands each failed message to the
one tagged for it, with the chain-conflict strategy as fallback. A listener ends a
delivery whose retries ran out, once, under the tenant. A code is never transmitted
at or after its send window, on a retry or a replay.

feat(notification): a stale invitation or notice ends NOT_NEEDED instead of being sent

Every purpose declares what it is checked against just before sending (ADR-0079
section 2.5). Comments on late sends now describe the notice's real retry span.
